stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest LLM releases.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Apple will limit Mac disk access as AI agents ‘substantially’ increase risk
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is implementing new restrictions on 'full disk access' for macOS.
The change is a direct response to security risks amplified by the rise of AI agents.
The new controls aim to ensure users intentionally grant this high level of application access.

stories.title: US arrests tech CEO accused of smuggling $300M in Nvidia chips into China
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A US tech CEO has been arrested for allegedly smuggling $300M worth of Nvidia chips into China.
The incident highlights ongoing and persistent issues regarding the export control and smuggling of advanced AI hardware.
This news underscores the geopolitical tensions surrounding high-end semiconductor technology between the US and China.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes standard ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors.
Indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's Llama family of models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as shown by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in animating 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Introduces GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to approximate complex animations.
Replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a lightweight shallow coefficient predictor for real-time performance.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations by moving beyond knowledge-based or high-level agentic tasks to focus on precise CLI command generation.
Features 'runtime-free verifiable rewards,' suggesting a novel approach to accurately and safely assessing tool invocation correctness.

stories.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
stories.author: Kaiming He
bullet_points: Introduces VISTA, a visual harness designed to unlock the reasoning potential of multimodal AI models.
VISTA provides general-purpose multimodal models with long-horizon vision capabilities in interactive environments.
The system features a lossless visual memory, allowing the model to actively retrieve and maintain past environmental observations.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in real-time animation of 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method that approximates complex animation using a linear combination of blendshapes.
Replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a much faster, shallow coefficient predictor for efficient avatar animation.

stories.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research addresses the fundamental question of whether LLMs possess true structural mathematical understanding, rather than just pattern matching.
The paper introduces the concept of 'Mathematical Primitive' as a new diagnostic tool to probe LLM capabilities in mathematics.
The findings aim to systematically diagnose current LLM limitations and guide future improvements through post-training techniques.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama now integrates support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution for making decisions based on text.
The decision models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta has open-sourced the code for its Muse AI agent.
This allows developers to create custom 'Muse gadgets' using the AI.
Suggested use cases include integrating Muse onto E Ink displays or HDMI sticks.

stories.title: Netflix is pivoting away from prestige
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Netflix is reportedly shifting its content strategy away from high-profile, prestige productions.
This pivot is evidenced by the streamer ending multiyear production deals with notable directors.
The change signals a potential strategic divergence from previous content investment models.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
stories.author: Allison Johnson
bullet_points: OpenAI has unveiled a new agent platform named Dots.
The platform is positioned as enterprise software, though it possesses consumer-like capabilities (e.g., ordering food).
The article contrasts Dots with Meta's Muse, suggesting Dots have a more 'workplace software' feel.

stories.title: Rivian’s sales pop as the company’s big R2 bet starts to pay off
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Rivian reported significant growth in Q3, with production increasing by 85% year-over-year.
Vehicle deliveries saw a substantial jump of 45% compared to the previous year.
The positive sales figures suggest that Rivian's strategy, including the upcoming R2 model, is gaining traction.

stories.title: Dots get up in Muse’s business
stories.author: Jacob Kastrenakes
bullet_points: OpenAI has released 'Dots,' a new product positioned as a business-focused alternative to Muse.
Dots is priced at a minimum of $100 per month, indicating a B2B or professional focus.
The product appears to offer similar creative capabilities to Muse but is geared toward commercial use.

stories.title: Amazon’s $1B plan to combat data center backlash draws more backlash
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Amazon has a $1B initiative aimed at addressing negative public sentiment regarding its data centers.
The company received mixed reactions, being praised for ending Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs).
However, Amazon faced criticism for allegedly minimizing the environmental impact and pollution associated with its data centers.

stories.title: Lyft settles landmark driver misclassification lawsuit for $272.5M
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: Lyft has settled a significant lawsuit regarding the misclassification of its drivers.
The settlement amount reached $272.5 million.
The resolution faces criticism from groups claiming drivers are owed substantially more.

stories.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces RPG, a framework for autonomous self-improvement in embodied agents (robots).
The system improves robot execution capabilities without requiring updates to the underlying model weights.
RPG works by identifying skills from offline data, generating simulation practice tasks, and using execution feedback.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of AI systems to identify inspiring prior research papers.
The benchmark is built using expert annotations from researchers who can pinpoint which past works were crucial to their own projects.
This addresses a key limitation in current AI research: the ability to sense which buried prior ideas are relevant for novel problem-solving.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
The framework aims to improve topological preservation and reduce generation costs for complex 3D shapes.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) as an alternative to discrete diffusion models.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independent token sampling bottleneck found in discrete diffusion models.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, which maintains statistical dependencies during parallel decoding.

stories.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
stories.author: Chongyang Ma
bullet_points: Introduces DMAD (Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation) for faster visual generation.
DMAD reframes distribution matching as a classification problem to learn log-density ratios directly.
It aims to overcome the computational overhead associated with traditional distribution matching methods.

stories.title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
stories.author: Tolga Birdal
bullet_points: Introduces Higher-order Grammar Representation (HGR) to address limitations in molecular learning models.
HGR is designed to explicitly encode complex, higher-order molecular topologies like ring systems and recurring motifs.
The framework aims to overcome the computational demands and decoding difficulties of existing higher-order representations.

stories.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
stories.author: Stella X. Yu
bullet_points: The research proposes using predicted embeddings as a conditioning mechanism in diffusion transformers for image generation.
The core methodology involves training a Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA) model to forecast subsequent continuous embeddings.
This approach leverages the sequential nature of image generation (noisy to clean) to train the predictive model.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
The approach aims to improve topological awareness and reduce generation costs compared to existing token-based methods.

stories.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: TACO is a new optimizer designed to reduce the memory overhead associated with full-parameter fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs).
It addresses the memory limitations of current LLM fine-tuning by introducing a Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse update mechanism.
TACO aims to improve upon existing methods (like Muon) that either compress state or alter update geometry, while maintaining performance parity with AdamW.

stories.title: Cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs are exactly solvable: a Feynman-Kac tilt replaces learned control
stories.author: Akshay Balsubramani
bullet_points: The research addresses the problem of finding a generalized Schrödinger bridge on graphs that incorporates a state-visitation cost.
It introduces a theoretical simplification: the cost-augmented bridge can be solved exactly by applying a Feynman-Kac tilt to the reference process.
This exact solution eliminates the need for complex learning methods, such as temporal-difference penalties, previously used to handle the cost.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) as an alternative to discrete diffusion models.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independent token sampling bottleneck found in discrete diffusion models during parallel decoding.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, which is hypothesized to maintain inter-token statistical dependencies.

stories.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of step-size selection in large-scale LLM fine-tuning optimization.
Introduces Zero-and-First-Order optimization (ZFO) to decouple direction selection from step-size.
ZFO uses first-order methods for direction finding, then employs zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size determination.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or end-to-end tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
Features runtime-free verifiable rewards, suggesting a focus on rigorous and automated testing of command syntax and correctness.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of AI systems to find inspiring prior research.
The benchmark leverages expert knowledge by having researchers annotate which past papers influenced their own work.
This addresses a key gap in AI research: the ability to sense which buried prior ideas are relevant for advancing new scientific problems.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independent token sampling bottleneck present in discrete diffusion models, which limits bidirectional reasoning.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, allowing for better capture of inter-token statistical dependencies.

stories.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Xin Dong
bullet_points: Introduces AutoCompact, a method to train coding agents to intelligently manage context in long-horizon software engineering tasks.
Addresses the challenge of stale context in agents performing complex, multi-step tasks like repository-level coding.
The agent learns not just to avoid context overflow, but to decide *when* and *how* to compact and resume its working state.

stories.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
stories.author: Juan S. Santillana
bullet_points: Keyword-matching benchmarks can falsely credit small language models with tool-use capabilities they do not actually possess.
The paper proposes a set of 'cheap diagnostics' to rigorously test and validate tool-use claims in smaller LLMs.
The study demonstrates this issue using matched-architecture Spanish security language models, highlighting the limitations of lenient evaluation metrics.

stories.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: The paper investigates improving frontier model capabilities beyond standard Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL).
It challenges the conventional view that RL is superior for generalization while SFT suffers from weak generalization and catastrophic forgetting.
The proposed method, 'Finetuning with Sampling,' aims to enhance learning efficiency, particularly by leveraging off-policy expert data.

stories.title: Argo-Bench: Evaluating Data Agents on Enterprise-Scale Workflows
stories.author: Joseph J Ma
bullet_points: Argo-Bench introduces a new evaluation framework for data agents designed for complex, enterprise-scale workflows.
It addresses the limitations of existing text-to-SQL benchmarks, which only test query generation and often have flawed answer keys.
The framework uses public datasets to simulate real-world scenarios requiring reasoning across multiple tables and statistical analysis.

stories.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
stories.author: Spyros Gidaris
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Where-OPD,' a method applying on-policy self-distillation to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
This technique aims to improve MLLM reasoning by using a self-supervised distillation process, which is an underexplored area for MLLMs.
It addresses limitations in current methods that rely only on localized visual cues (like image crops) for fine-grained perception.

stories.title: Court agrees with EFF: Utah's VPN law demands a technical impossibility
stories.author: hn_acker
bullet_points: A court has ruled in favor of the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) regarding a law in Utah.
The core issue involves Utah's VPN legislation, which reportedly imposes a technically impossible requirement.
This case highlights ongoing legal and technical conflicts surrounding privacy and encryption in US states.

stories.title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI until now
stories.author: PaulHoule
bullet_points: AI models previously struggled with the game Stratego due to hidden information.
Recent research, linked to Nature and arXiv, details the breakthrough in AI solving this complex game.
The study highlights the challenges of AI in partially observable, strategic environments.

stories.title: From the creator of Redis; run LLM locally with ds4
stories.author: fibo
bullet_points: A new tool, ds4, allows users to run Large Language Models (LLMs) locally.
The tool is developed by someone who previously worked on Redis, suggesting technical depth.
This addresses the growing trend of local, private LLM deployment.

stories.title: The Four Horsemen of Agentic Coding
stories.author: distantprovince.substack.com via guillego
bullet_points: The article discusses 'Agentic Coding,' a growing trend in AI development.
It frames the key components or challenges of this paradigm as the 'Four Horsemen.'
The topic suggests a shift towards more autonomous and complex AI software development workflows.

stories.title: Building Sarrera: Self-Hosted Enterprise AI Inference Gateway with RBAC, Token Quotas & Telemetry
stories.author: marioezquerro
bullet_points: Details the construction of a self-hosted, private AI inference gateway for enterprise use.
Leverages specific tools like LiteLLM, Caddy, Langfuse, and Open WebUI for implementation.
Features advanced enterprise controls including Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and token quotas.
